newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares rebound on rate cut expectations.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares rebound on rate cut expectations.

text.p: Greek shares rebounded on quiet trading on Wednesday by hopes of further rate cuts following the success of Tuesday's Treasury paper issue, market watchers said.
"The market is reacting favourably to the prospect of further rate cuts," said Yanna Tziovara, assistant fund manager with Allianz Mutual Funds.
"I expect the market in the coming few sessions to consolidate at slightly higher levels as there is not a great deal of fresh funds chasing stocks at the moment," she added.
Greece on Tuesday raised about 600 billion drachmas from the sale of 12-month T-bills and 200 billion from two-year zeros.
The two-year zero coupon featured an unchanged gross yield of 10.1 percent and the 12-month T-bills carried a gross rate of 10.3 percent, down 20 basis points from the previous issue.
The market was not spooked by reports of negligible 1996 profitability in state Commercial and Ionian banks, taking a positive view on their management's effort to cleanse their balance sheets.
Ionian Bank said its 1996 profit before tax and provisions was down 69 percent to 5.0 billion drachmas, foregoing a dividend for fiscal 1996.
The Athens general share index advanced 1.67 percent or 22.64 points from Tuesday's 1,352.46, settling at 1,375.10. Turnover grew slightly to 15.6 billion drachmas on volume of 4.2 million shares.
Banking stocks continued to lead the broader market trend, like they have done since the begining of the year, rising 1.79 percent.
National Mortgage closed 3.7 percent higher at 20,285 and ErgoBank strengthened 1.9 percent to 16,590. OTE closed past the 6,000 barrier, registering a 2.8 percent gain.
Advancers led decliners 157 to 55 with 35 issues unchanged on 247 traded.
